items.title: Scott Hamilton interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995
items.q: I’ve spent a lot of time hanging out with them, especially the guys from the original Basie band, you know the ones I’ve known, Buck Clayton was a good friend, and Buddy Tate, Sweets Edison, Jo Jones was a good friend.

ctx.x: Well that’s great. Tell us, talk a little about you said you had not necessarily played with but you had heard the Basie band.

I’ve been a sort of, I mean that’s very special to me. If I were to have to give up all music except for one band, I would have to say give me Count Basie and I could live with that. I think that would do it. Because for me it represents everything that I consider important in music. And I’ve always aligned myself with members of Basie band’s past, and tried to become friendly with the guys. So I’ve spent a lot of time hanging out with them, especially the guys from the original Basie band, you know the ones I’ve…
band too. I don’t know, nothing’s coming to mind at the moment but as I said over the years it’s been very important music to me.

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: I had a little set-to with a radio disc jockey in Boston. He was asking me what I thought about Scott Hamilton.

ctx.x: Yeah. You know, they have something. But at the same time, there is a very sort of subtle kind of prejudice to promote them.

Well, I'll tell you why. It was a cold sort of thing. Now, Frankie Trumbauer's playing would never thrill you like Lester's playing. There was a certain warmth -- it's a certain warmth in the blacks' playing that's like a magnet that will make you -- you know, it's something -- like Scott Hamilton, I had a little set-to with a radio disc jockey in Boston.
